title: Migration 39 — counterparty organisations and the buyer role
description: Applies migration 39, runs VERIFY A-G, then rolls back on a disposable PostgreSQL 18 cluster. Migration 39 introduces the first non-farm counterparty identity in the schema: organisations (farm | buyer | laboratory | carrier | broker | internal), organisation_memberships, and the 'buyer' value on profiles.role. VERIFY section E is the first in this corpus to SET ROLE authenticated and re-query, because every other VERIFY runs as the table owner and therefore BYPASSES row level security -- a reversed policy would verify green. E observes the double-blind rule from both sides plus an identity-less caller. The rollback refuses to drop non-empty tables without an explicit SET LOCAL organisations.rollback_destructive opt-in, and deliberately does NOT narrow compliance_audit_log's action CHECK back: that log is append-only and TRUNCATE-hardened, so narrowing it would invalidate history the platform guarantees is immutable. On a disposable cluster the tables are empty at rollback time, so the default non-destructive path drops them and postRollback asserts their removal.

verify.note: All seven sections assert. A structure, B the widened role vocabulary (including that it still rejects an unknown role -- widening must not become 'anything goes'), C the RLS posture, D seven invalid organisation states each of which must be rejected (including NaN ownership, which a lower-bound-only CHECK would admit because PostgreSQL sorts NaN above every real number), E the behavioural double-blind proof as role authenticated, F audit emission with verification changes as a distinct action, G that anon holds nothing. NOT read-only: E and F insert fixtures, so the whole file is wrapped in BEGIN..ROLLBACK and must not be run against Production under the change freeze.
